title: Finite Monoid Computations and a Uniform Generalized Star-Height Bound
main_claim: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression (with complement) of star height at most 13 over the same alphabet. The proof parses words into a prefix code of episodes. Each episode is bounded, or is a bounded part, then a periodic run, then a bounded tail, so every per-episode test has height ≤1. The monoid action along episode sequences is then recovered through 12 nested prefix/suffix split steps, each adding one star: 2 outer splits (prediction trials and periodic windows) and 2 per residual witness type for 5 types (aligned decoding, primary trial and secondary decision-tree measurement).

issues.location: sec:geometry, Lemma periodic-overlap (ii), as applied in Lemma periodic-split availability
issues.description: Part (ii) is stated for a symmetric markerless window [z-H,z+H]. It is applied to the asymmetric window [z-H, z+H+2R_2]. Re-centering at z+R_2 with halfwidth H+R_2 gives exactly the needed run, so this is only an imprecise citation.
issues.evidence: S_2 (eq. S2) asks for a markerless [z_λ-H, z_λ+H+2R_2]; the proof cites the lemma for short-period blocks from z-H+d_∘ onward without stating the re-centering.

sibling_notes: No sibling reports existed in family 134 when I checked. The intro cites companion papers (OpenAIHeight4, OpenAIHeight3) claiming bounds 4 and 3, but says this proof does not depend on them, and I found no circular dependence: every lemma used is proved in this paper.
